name: Auroboro
backstory: Led the raid that took the tollhouse from Terfila's blockade in a single night, years ago; still counted the decisive hand behind Gorff's hold on the crossing road.

experience.text: Had a child with Mekestros, named Mekoboro.
Had a child with Aurebalo, named Aureboro.
Heard that Mekestros and Aureluko now have a child, Mekaluko.
Heard that Khaus and Mekoboro now have a child, Khaoboro.
Heard that Khaubalo and Mekestros now have a child, Khaubestro.
Heard that Aurebalo and Merluko now have a child, Aurebako.
Heard that Aurebalo and Mekoboro now have a child, Aurekobo.
Heard that Mekestros and Khaubalo now have a child, Khaumestro.
Heard that Mekestros and Khaubalo now have a child, Mekhaubo.
Heard that Aurebalo and Khaoboro now have a child, Aurekhobo.
Heard that Khaubalo and Merluko now have a child, Merkhaubo.

criterion.standard: counts what the tollhouse cost to take above what it's worth having now
criterion.wasted_life: letting the night he broke that blockade get told as something smaller than it was
criterion.origin: collision between his backstory (led the raid himself) and crossing_toll_dispute itself
criterion.trusts: a story that's been carried and retold and still holds together
criterion.distrusts: a record that insists on a precision no one who was actually there ever needed

routines.routine_actions: still walks the tollhouse's own stretch of the transit route most mornings, checks the crews on duty, corrects any traveler who gets the story of that night wrong

needs: a way to be formally credited for the raid in something more permanent than a ledger entry
arc.premise: Auroboro wants the tollhouse itself to carry some permanent mark of the raid that took it - a plaque, a stone, something a traveler passing through has to see - not just a line in Gorff's own ledger that Terfila keeps insisting isn't the whole story.
